It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law

15 . As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
16. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.

The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which she had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by her in the accident.
The "non-pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards her treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2025.07.14 16:02:02 +0530 of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc. and the non-pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where she was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate her or to put her almost in the same place or position where she could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating her is also not to reward her or to make her rich in an unjust manner.

It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the Malti Devi (I)(Fir299/2024/Lahori ... vs Daya Ram (Sbi Gen. (iii) Loss of income 20.
As per DAR, petitioner was 79 years of age at the time of accident.
The medical records of petitioner reflect that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries which resulted into 17% permanent physical disability with respect to left lower limb.

The above documents are sufficient to uphold the claim of the petitioner to the effect that she was unable to resume her PANKAJ Date:
SHARMA 2025.07.14 16:02:12 +0530 vocation since the date of accident.
In view of the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, it could be safely assumed that the petitioner has become unfit for work for about 06 months due to the injuries.
As per DAR, the petitioner was doing self work at the time of accident.

In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the petitioner, it would be appropriate that the monthly income of petitioner be assessed as per the minimum wages payable to an unskilled person in Delhi as on the date of accident(petitioner being an ordinary resident of Delhi at the relevant time).
As per relevant notification, the minimum wages admissible to an unskilled person as on 28.05.2024 in Delhi were Rs.17,988/-.

As such, the petitioner is held entitled to a sum of Rs.1,07,928/- (Rs.17,988/- X 06).
The said sum is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
(iv) Loss of future earnings due to disability 21.
Petitioner claimed that she has become permanently disabled after the accident and could not perform her work for months.
Admittedly, petitioner has suffered 17% permanent physical impairment with respect to left lower limb.
From the facts, it is evident that the petitioner was selling pulses, dry fruits etc. and after the accident, she has suffered 17% permanent physical impairment in her left lower limb.

Therefore, it is apposite to note that petitioner has become Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2025.07.14 16:02:14 +0530 incapacitated to work following physical disability.
Due to injury, she has become permanent disabled to the extent of 17% in the vital part of the body i.e. the leg due to which she is unable to sit properly which has directly effected her vocation.
Since she is a vendor selling food items on pavement, the said disability would be an impediment in her day to day working thereby diminishing her earning prospects.
In these circumstances and in the absence of any material to the contrary, it would be prudent to assess her functional disability to a extent of 17%.
This Tribunal has already assumed the monthly income of petitioner to be Rs.17,988/- at the relevant time.
As far as the age of petitioner at the time of accident is concerned, she was 79 years.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
8. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
There is nothing on record which betrays any falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW-1.
As such, it could be safely held that the oral testimony of PW-1 is reliable and trustworthy.
Therefore, it has come out that petitioner Malti Devi suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant time, R-1 was driving the offending vehicle in rash and negligent manner in a high speed and hit the petitioner and petitioner got injured.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/ sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
16. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.
The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which she had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by her in the accident.
The "non-pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.
It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where she was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate her or to put her almost in the same place or position where she could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating her is also not to reward her or to make her rich in an unjust manner.
It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the Malti Devi (I)(Fir299/2024/Lahori ... vs Daya Ram (Sbi Gen. Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on her earning capacity.

As per DAR, the petitioner was doing self work at the time of accident.
In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the petitioner, it would be appropriate that the monthly income of petitioner be assessed as per the minimum wages payable to an unskilled person in Delhi as on the date of accident(petitioner being an ordinary resident of Delhi at the relevant time).
Petitioner claimed that she has become permanently disabled after the accident and could not perform her work for months.
Admittedly, petitioner has suffered 17% permanent physical impairment with respect to left lower limb.
Due to injury, she has become permanent disabled to the extent of 17% in the vital part of the body i.e. the leg due to which she is unable to sit properly which has directly effected her vocation.
Since she is a vendor selling food items on pavement, the said disability would be an impediment in her day to day working thereby diminishing her earning prospects.
In these circumstances and in the absence of any material to the contrary, it would be prudent to assess her functional disability to a extent of 17%.
This Tribunal has already assumed the monthly income of petitioner to be Rs.17,988/- at the relevant time.
